Cara (Marketing): Hey runtime team — prepping a webinar and launch post. Need a small, reproducible smoke run and a mapping from bench metrics to marketing KPIs. Can you help? :wave:
Liam (Growth PM): tl;dr: we need p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and an estimated $/1000 tokens for each model variant (fp16, int8, q4_0). Also want sample payloads we can use in slides.
Sam (eng-runtime): Yep — can do. What's the target models and typical prompt lengths for the webinar demos?
Cara (Marketing): Primary demo is code-completion + short chat. Seq len ~256 for code, ~128 for chat. Traffic profile: 50 concurrent users in the smoke run, but we just need a 5-10 minute sweep.
Anya (eng-ml): For quantized variants I'll need model names and weights. Are we testing Redwood-Open-1.2 and community-llama-3-70b or only one?
Cara (Marketing): Let's include Redwood-Open-1.2 fp16 + q4_0, and community-llama-3-70b int8. If runtime can't do 70b quantized on the infra we can drop it.
Sam (eng-runtime): Got it. Proposed quick plan: 1) smoke job: 5m steady, 50 qps burst, 2) configs: batch_size=8, max_tokens=256, kv_cache=true, 3) collect p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and a simple cost-estimate using our accounting model.
Sam (eng-runtime): Please provide 3 canonical payloads (code short, code long, chat). Example payload snippet to use:```json
{"model":"redwood-open-1.2","input":"def fib(n):\n    # compute fib...","max_tokens":128,"temperature":0.2}```
Liam (Growth PM): For marketing we need a table: model | variant | p50 | p95 | tok/sec | est $/1k tok | note. Also one or two sample transcripts (short) for the hero slide.
Cara (Marketing): Can you also include guidance on what changed between fp16 and q4_0 in terms of output quality (if you see regressions) so we can call that out?
Anya (eng-ml): We'll run a tiny eval set of 40 prompts concurrently against the three variants and flag any >5% regression in exact match or code compilation for the code sample.
Sam (eng-runtime): Scheduling smoke run now. bench-bot: job queued (id: jb-8242). Expect results in ~3 hours.
bench-bot: Job jb-8242 status: queued -> running on shard-a (logs: https://internal-bench/redwood/jobs/jb-8242).
Liam (Growth PM): Great. Can you post the raw CSV and a sanitized CSV (no customer data) so marketing can generate charts?
Sam (eng-runtime): We'll output raw CSV and a sanitized copy (strip prompt text, keep lengths and IDs). Also we'll include the curl commands to reproduce locally. Example:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-open-1.2","input":"...","max_tokens":128}'```
Cara (Marketing): Timeline check — webinar materials need final numbers by EOD tomorrow. Realistic?
Sam (eng-runtime): If bench starts now, yes. We may need to extend for an extra rerun if we see variance. Will ping if that happens.
Anya (eng-ml): If any variant shows >10% latency variance between runs, we'll run a 30m stability sweep and include confidence intervals.
Cara (Marketing): Awesome — thanks. Please drop the sanitized CSV + KPI table in #marketing when ready and tag me. :pray:
Sam (eng-runtime): Will do. Adding a short README with methodology: what we measured, config used, and how cost was estimated. I'll include the exact kernel/quant config we used for reproducibility.
Liam (Growth PM): One final ask — can we get a 1-line caveat we can use in the press copy about synthetic vs production traffic?
Sam (eng-runtime): Sure: "Numbers are from controlled smoke runs using synthetic workloads; production performance depends on prompt distribution and concurrency patterns." I'll toss that into the README.
Cara (Marketing): Perfect. Thanks team!
bench-bot: Job jb-8242 status: completed (summary: 50 users, 5m, 3 variants). CSVs at https://internal-bench/redwood/jobs/jb-8242/results.zip
